faehigkeiten.grund: Auslieferung wird je Abruf neu zusammengesetzt (adswizz vergibt je Abruf eine listeningSessionID, AIS leitet ueber hash_redirect um, Last-Modified liegt nur 2 s vor dem Abruf, Abruf laeuft ueber den Werbedienst simplecastaudio.com) - Byte-Offsets veralten (bei dynamischer Auslieferung sofort, gemessen 19.08.2026) und die Zeitachse verschiebt sich mit (eine Folge war 57 s kuerzer als 3,5 h zuvor), deshalb sind auch Sprungmarken in Sekunden unsicher

einzeiler: Colman Domingo joins the podcast to discuss his career, stage roots, and creative process.
kurzfassung: Colman Domingo talks about his extensive career in theater, film, and television, sharing insights into his creative process and memorable roles. He reflects on the challenges of early industry struggles and how finding the right support shifted his trajectory. The conversation also explores his transition into directing and the value of embracing imperfections in artistic work.
stichpunkte: Discussion of critical reception and how social media crowdsourcing impacts box office success
Colman Domingo's approach to humanizing complex historical figures like Joe Jackson
Reflections on his early career, including working multiple side jobs while performing off-Broadway
The pivotal moment when a college acting teacher encouraged him to pursue the profession
Almost leaving the entertainment industry entirely before landing a life-changing role in Fear the Walking Dead
Transitioning into directing and producing television episodes
The philosophy of embracing artistic imperfections and moving into a truth-telling season of life

clips.hook: When your taste in film brings zero money and terrible reviews
clips.text: A reflection on discovering a critically panned and financially unsuccessful movie that nonetheless resonated deeply with personal taste, leading to humorous self-doubt about one's own judgment.

clips.hook: I beat him all the way to the bank
clips.text: Recounting a striking interview quote from Joe Jackson regarding harsh discipline and its role in achieving immense financial success.

clips.hook: Why memorizing 90% beforehand keeps the performance raw
clips.text: An explanation of why memorizing the vast majority of lines before day one allows an actor to remain loose, collaborative, and receptive to on-set changes.

clips.hook: Entering the truth-telling season of your mid-fifties
clips.text: The realization that reaching one's mid-fifties marks a shift toward storytelling and eventually a truth-telling season where saying no without qualifiers becomes liberating.

clips.hook: A personal breakthrough after forgetting lines on stage
clips.text: Realizing that forgetting lines during a one-man show about family stemmed from merely performing rather than truly living the emotional material.
